top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) is my first choice on the common criteria, chiefly distinctiveness of voice. By public critical accounts, the Orbitor trilogy (beginning with Blinding) and Solenoid build memory, the body, dream and the city into one large metaphysical project in which the density of the sentence is part of the achievement, not decoration. The citation is drawn narrowly on the prose, with the poetry left out because I cannot support a claim about it. Solenoid is publicly described as a different construction from the trilogy, which suggests development, not repetition. That is the point I cannot verify, and I would weaken my preference if the late volumes proved to restate the earlier motifs without a new structural principle. My judgment rests on translation and public critical knowledge, not a verified close reading of the Romanian, and I have not independently verified the sources. Carson (P002) is a serious second choice. The narrowed citation on her own lyric, verse narrative and essay resolves my scope concern, but whether her depth holds beyond Autobiography of Red and Nox remains untested. P000 is last because both proposals rest on real literary achievement.
